text.p: 3Com Corp. Tuesday reported higher sales and profits for the latest quarter, reflecting strong demand for its equipment that links computers into networks.

3Com said net income rose to $89.2 million, or 48 cents a share, in its fourth quarter ended in May, from $24.5 million, or 16 cents a share on a fully diluted basis, a year earlier when the results included a pretax charge of $53 million, or 30 cents a share. Sales rose 26 percent to $830 million from $660 million.
3com's profit was in line with expectations on Wall Street but the company's stock fell in after-hours trade as some investors were hoping for a stronger-than-expected quarter.
Traders said the computer networking company fell to $48.50 in after-hours dealing. It had risen $1.50 to $49.75 during regular trading on Nasdaq.

"Our fourth quarter caps another year of growth in 3Com's revenues, earnings, market share and competitive stature," said Chairman Eric Benhamou. "Our business is being driven by customer requirements for complete networking systems ... both for the local area and wide area network."
Sales of switches, hubs and other network gear rose 20 percent to $473 million. Sales of network adapters increased 35 percent to $349.6 million.
3Com's results do not include earnings from U.S. Robotics Corp. The merger between the two companies was approved earlier this month.

Net income for the year ended in May rose to $374 million, or $2.01 a share, from $178 million, or $1.00 a share, the previous year. The latest period includes a $6.6 million charge related to the acquisition of OnStream Networks Inc.
Sales jumped 35 percent to a record $3.1 billion from $2.3 billion in fiscal 1996.
